$comment: The reasons a verdict lists (agentcake/detect/verdict_text.py fills them in). Each has the layer it belongs to, its evidence grade (env_rules.json legend: measured, project-claim, source, inferred) its English text (what it means) and, when it has one, its detail (what was seen, in technical words: the second line under the text); {placeholders} in both are filled from the reason's facts, which the verdict keeps so that a reason is worded anew each time it is shown (verdict_text.words: facts named half, method, other_method, basis, signals, marker and signature name a phrase of this file, agent_markers.json or webbotauth.json), {product} is the product name (product.json) and $missing stands in for a fact that is not known. tone is how the interface marks it (agent, human or none: a fact for neither). Layers are the interface's (web/src/data/schema/session.schema.json: name, verify, environment, behavior) plus exclusion (rule 0) and weak (weak signals). An environment rule's hit is listed under the rule's own id with the rule's title and detail (env_rules.json); a Web Bot Auth result's own words come from webbotauth.json and fill {signature} and {signature_detail}; an agent product's indicator fills {marker} and {marker_detail} from agent_markers.json. Interface text (English only; Human / Agent / Mixed / Not sure / Bot).

behavior_basis.rules_unnamed: enough agent-like behavior in the clicks and keystrokes
behavior_basis.active_move_rate: less pointer movement than a human usually makes
behavior_basis.teleport_clicks: clicks that come immediately after the pointer jumps
behavior_basis.typing_cadence: typing with a steadier rhythm than human typing
behavior_basis.fast_arrivals: pointer movement that doesn't slow down near click targets

methods.automation-trace: code that the tool leaves in the page

exclude.prefetch.text: Server middleware data isn't counted for pages that are requested in advance, such as page {page}.
exclude.prefetch.detail: The browser requested this page as a {purpose}. Its request included the header Sec-Purpose: {purpose}.

exclude.never-shown.text: Page {page} was prepared in advance but never shown, so it isn't counted.
exclude.never-shown.detail: The browser prerendered this page but never showed it.

exclude.all.text: Every page in this session was prepared in advance and never shown, so the session isn't counted as a visit.
exclude.all.detail: The browser prerendered every page but never showed any of them.

name.ua.detail: The User-Agent of {half} includes {name}, which is listed as {kind_label}.

name.ua-browser.detail: The User-Agent of {half} includes {name}, which is listed as {kind_label}.

name.ua-generic.text: {name} is a general-purpose tool, not a specific agent product.

name.ua-conflict.text: The visitor reports several product names at once.

name.ua-hint.text: The browser's User-Agent matches a known pattern of forged or malformed values. This match alone isn't enough to show that the User-Agent is forged.

name.platform.text: The browser reports the same platform that {name} uses.

name.signer.text: The request identifies {signer}, which signs requests for {name}.

name.unknown-signer.text: The request identifies a signer that isn't included in this release.
name.unknown-signer.detail: The Signature-Agent header on {half} shows {signer}. This release doesn't include that signer.

name.disagree.text: The visitor reports names that don't match each other.

name.signer-mismatch.text: The request identifies one signer, but it's signed by another.
name.signer-mismatch.detail: The Signature-Agent header shows {claimed}, but the signature belongs to {signer}.

name.outranked.text: This visit is shown as {name} because the method that found this name has the highest priority.
name.outranked.detail: The name {other} came from {other_method}, but names from {method} take priority.

name.from-trace.detail: This trace belongs to {name}. A product's traces can change when the product updates.

verify.signature-forged.text: The signature for {name} fails verification. Visits that fail this check are treated as impersonation.

verify.signature-proxy.text: The signature couldn't be verified, possibly because a proxy in front of your site changed the request. The visit isn't marked as impersonation.
verify.signature-proxy.detail: {signature_detail} The signature covers {components}. A proxy in front of your site can rewrite these parts.

verify.ip-range.text: Verified: the IP address is in a range that {operator} publishes for {name}.

verify.ip-agent-range.text: The IP address is in a range that {operator} publishes for its agents.

verify.ip-bot-range.text: The IP address belongs to a range that {operator} publishes for its crawlers. The visitor doesn't report a name.

verify.ip-mismatch.text: The IP address isn't in a range that {operator} publishes for {name}. Visits that fail this check are treated as impersonation.

verify.rdns-mismatch.text: A reverse DNS lookup of the IP address doesn't match {name}. This counts as impersonation.
verify.rdns-mismatch.detail: A reverse DNS lookup doesn't confirm {name}.

verify.no-range.text: {product} can't verify {name}, so the name is marked as self-reported.
verify.no-range.detail: {name} doesn't publish an IP address range or a key that {product} can check.

verify.local.text: In local mode, names are self-reported and aren't verified.
verify.local.detail: In local mode, all visits come from 127.0.0.1, so names can't be checked against IP address ranges.

verify.no-address.text: Names are self-reported because the visitor's IP address wasn't available.
verify.no-address.detail: Without the IP address, the visit can't be checked against published IP address ranges.

verify.address-cdn.text: {product} couldn't verify names by IP address, so names are marked as self-reported.
verify.address-cdn.detail: {product} checked the last {sessions} sessions with an address. {cdn} of these sessions came from published CDN IP ranges. This usually means that a CDN or proxy in front of {product} hides each visitor's address.

env.automated.text: The browser shows signs of automation but doesn't show which tool. This can be an AI tool working for a human or a script.
env.automated.detail: Automation markers are present, but none of them identifies the tool.

env.cloud-browser.text: The visit runs in a cloud browser that doesn't identify its operator.

env.extension-unnamed.text: A browser extension acted on this page, but its name isn't known.

env.soft-alone.text: These signs also appear when humans use DevTools, privacy tools, or similar features. On their own, these signs don't identify automation.

behavior.agent.text: The behavior in this session is typical of an agent.

behavior.turns.text: A human and an agent took turns in this session.

behavior.turns-runs.text: A human and an agent took turns in this session.

behavior.human.text: The behavior in this session is typical of a human.

behavior.one-kind.text: The behavior model can't identify an agent from one kind of agent-like behavior alone.
behavior.one-kind.detail: The behavior model detected agent-like behavior only in {kind}. For this session, the model needs two or more independent kinds of agent-like behavior to identify an agent.

behavior.unsure.text: The behavior model can't tell whether a human or an agent acted in this session.

behavior.indicator.text: All actions while {marker} was visible count as agent actions.

behavior.indicator-tail.text: Actions while {marker} was visible count as agent actions until the agent stopped.
behavior.indicator-tail.detail: {marker_detail} The indicator stays on for a few seconds after the agent stops. The behavior model classified the actions after the agent stopped.

behavior.handoff.text: The {to} took over from the {from} at {at}.

behavior.short-run.text: This run of actions by the {who} is too short to count. The {who} isn't treated as taking part in this session.
behavior.short-run.detail: The {who}'s run lasted {span} seconds and included {n} actions.

behavior.overruled.text: The behavior model classified this session as human. For this session, the classification is based on the signs of automation instead of the behavior model.

behavior.assistive.text: Assistive tools often navigate with the keyboard only, so this navigation isn't treated as agent behavior.
behavior.assistive.detail: The visitor uses only the keyboard to navigate and doesn't use a pointer.

behavior.local-agent.text: Only the behavior in this session is typical of an agent. This can happen when an agent runs on the visitor's own computer.
behavior.local-agent.detail: There's no agent trace in the page or the browser.

behavior.too-little-data.text: The behavior model doesn't classify this session because it has too few actions.
behavior.too-little-data.detail: The session has {n} actions, and the model needs at least {min}.

behavior.touch.text: The browser reports a phone or tablet, so the behavior model isn't used.

behavior.touch-not-claimed.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because the browser reports one on some pages but not on others.

behavior.touch-no-touch-points.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because the browser doesn't report any touch points on one of its pages.

behavior.touch-no-screen.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because the browser doesn't report a valid screen size on one of its pages.

behavior.touch-other-device.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because the User-Agent on one of its pages doesn't name one.
behavior.touch-other-device.detail: The device type used for this check is {device}. When the User-Agent names no device, only client hints that report Android can make it a phone or tablet, or, on a page that shows the desktop site, a web worker that reports an iPad, iPhone, or iPod. A page whose own worker didn't report uses the other pages' workers only if they all report the same device.

behavior.touch-screen-too-large.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because the screen on one of its pages is too large for the device type.
behavior.touch-screen-too-large.detail: The device type used for this check is {device}, and the screen is {w}x{h} CSS pixels. For this device type, {product} expects a short side of less than {min} CSS pixels.

behavior.touch-screen-too-small.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because the screen on one of its pages is too small for the device type.
behavior.touch-screen-too-small.detail: The device type used for this check is {device}, and the screen is {w}x{h} CSS pixels. For this device type, {product} expects a short side of at least {min} CSS pixels.

behavior.touch-no-worker.text: This visit can't be confirmed as a phone or tablet because no web worker reported the device on any of its pages.
behavior.touch-no-worker.detail: A page of this visit reports the platform {platform} and {points} touch points, more than any Mac has, as an iPad or iPhone showing the desktop site does. In that case, a web worker reports which device it is.

behavior.not-run-bot.text: This visitor is on the bot list, so the behavior model doesn't run.

crawler.like.text: This visit shows patterns that are typical of a crawler. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.

weak.timezone-country.text: The browser's time zone isn't used in the country of its IP address. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.
weak.timezone-country.detail: The time zone is {tz}, and the IP address country is {country}.

weak.language-country.text: The browser's language settings don't include the country of its IP address. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.
weak.language-country.detail: The languages are {languages}, and the IP address country is {country}.

weak.same-address.text: {n} sessions came from this IP address within {hours} hours. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.

weak.header-order.text: The requests don't match the browser that the User-Agent identifies. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.
weak.header-order.detail: The User-Agent header shows {browser}. The requests from cake.js list their headers in this order: {order}. {browser} doesn't use this order.

weak.display-change.text: The screen changed during the session. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.
weak.display-change.detail: The session reported color depths of {depths} and screen sizes of {sizes}.

weak.window-jump.text: The browser window moved a long distance on the screen without changing size. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.

weak.rhythm-pauses.text: Pauses before actions can suggest that an AI is reading the page before it acts. It's shown for information only and doesn't change the classification.
weak.rhythm-pauses.detail: {pct}% of the steps came after at least {seconds} seconds without input.
